takeaways: AMD beat on both lines: $2.09 of adjusted EPS vs $1.95 expected, and $13.38 billion in revenue vs $13.09 billion (LSEG). The company says revenue came in above the top of its own guidance.

The AI data center business is now the whole story: Data Center revenue nearly doubled to a record $8.5 billion (up 97%), driven by EPYC server CPUs and the launch of its Instinct MI450 AI GPUs. That segment is now 64% of sales, up from 47% a year ago (CNBC).

The guide is the headline: about $17 billion in Q4 revenue, roughly 66% growth from a year ago and 27% more than this quarter, vs a $16.2 billion analyst estimate (LSEG). The one nitpick: a ~55% gross margin guide, a hair under the 55.3% expected (StreetAccount).
Not everything is booming. Client and Gaming fell 8% to $3.7 billion; PC chips grew 7%, but gaming sales dropped 40% on weaker console (semi-custom) and graphics demand.

Reported (GAAP) EPS was $1.46, well below the adjusted $2.09, mainly because of a $1.1 billion non-cash hit from remeasuring warrants AMD gave to customers, which rises as AMD's stock price rises. Free cash flow was just $554 million as inventory jumped by about $3 billion ahead of the Q4 ramp.
verdict: AMD beat, then guided Q4 about $800 million above what Wall Street wanted, which is the chip-stock version of dropping the mic. The stock jumped after hours, undoing the last few days of 'AI is overspending' jitters. Fine print: the inventory pile and thin free cash flow mean the Q4 ramp actually has to show up.
